summary.text: Son of Poseidon and the Bithynian nymph Melie, king of the Bebrycians who forced strangers to box and was slain by Polydeuces when the Argonauts landed.

story.text: Apollonius tells how Amycus challenged all comers to box; Polydeuces, stung by the insult, stripped and killed the king. The Mariandyni, long at war with the Bebrycians, welcomed Polydeuces as a god for the deed.

The Bebrycian coast where Amycus ruled is named as a kingdom and boxing-ground for strangers, but no polis in our gazetteer is attested for his seat — Bebrycia remains a region on the Propontis shore, not a mapped city.
